purpose: Offer globally and individually disableable optional progress, resumability and logging through one immutable invocation policy, preserving independently required core outcomes.
first_step: Read #67's evidence and optional/core boundary, then run python -m unittest discover -s .reference -v. Inspect the eager-work and ignored-parent controls before deciding whether to adopt or adapt the helper in real owner bindings.

checks.environment: Python 3.12.14; Linux x86_64; Git 2.56.1; PyYAML 6.0.3. Local reference tests, not an admitted GitHub Actions performance profile.
checks.notes: 6 focused tests passed. Includes one actual isolated child process, lazy origin suppression, individual/all-off modes, required refusal/cancellation and two deliberately faulty bindings rejected by the same witness.

checks.command: Consumer integration, native crash/recovery qualification and GitHub Actions operation measurements
checks.reason: This handoff publishes a reference for independent decision; no consumer implementation or numerical contract was adopted.

limitations: Synthetic owner binding only. Real entrypoints, descendants, defaults and optional-work inventory are not discovered or qualified.

Optionality must follow real result/failure guarantees. Required acknowledged durability, effect identity, authorization, heartbeat/control work and mandatory evidence remain core. Historical barriers are not automatically mandatory.

Controls.call cannot prevent work done by the caller before invoking it; the eager-preparation counterexample demonstrates this integration risk. Child propagation is explicit cooperation, not a security sandbox.
No resumability algorithm, live-reconfiguration protocol, runtime allowance allocator, performance qualification or consumer-repository change is supplied.
The handling agent may accept, adapt, defer or reject this reference and must record its own Proffer disposition. Publication does not adopt the policy.
